claims.claim: Marcellus of Ancyra was the bishop of Ancyra in Galatia by about 314 and served at the Council of Nicaea in 325.
He lived approximately from 285/290 to about 374.
After Nicaea, Marcellus wrote a book against Asterius the Sophist, a defender of Arius, to refute Asterius’s teachings.
He was deposed by the synod of Constantinople in 336, a decision later reaffirmed by other eastern synods.
Marcellus appealed to Pope Julius I of Rome, submitted a letter and profession of faith in 341, and was cleared of the charges at a Roman synod.

No complete English translation of the fragments has ever been published, making new translations valuable for scholars of early Trinitarian theology.
